title: Real-World Python
intro: Learn the basic ideas of Real-World Python in simple English. Read the explanation and example first; the quiz asks only from the concepts taught here.

items.heading: Project structure
items.text: A real Python project is easier to maintain when related responsibilities are separated into clear files and folders.

items.heading: README
items.text: A README explains what a project does, how to install it and how to use it.

items.heading: Version control
items.text: Version control records changes to code so developers can review history, collaborate and restore earlier versions.

items.heading: Git
items.text: Git is a widely used version-control system for tracking source-code changes.

items.heading: Virtual environments
items.text: Projects commonly use virtual environments to isolate their dependencies from other projects.

items.heading: Configuration
items.text: Configuration contains values that control an application, such as a development setting or service URL.

items.heading: Environment variables
items.text: Environment variables let configuration values be supplied outside the source code, which is useful for deployment and secrets.

items.heading: CLI
items.text: A CLI, or command-line interface, lets a user control a program by typing commands in a terminal.

items.heading: Library
items.text: A library is reusable code that another program can import and use.

items.heading: Framework
items.text: A framework provides a structure and tools for building an application, often controlling part of the program flow.

items.heading: Documentation
items.text: Function and project documentation explains behavior, inputs, outputs and usage so other people can work with the code.

items.heading: Optimization
items.text: Measure a program before optimizing it so effort is focused on real bottlenecks rather than guesses.
